paper-comparison-svm-kernels-credit-2024.needs: No package name or hyperparameters given, so it's unclear whether the sdv-dev CTGAN package was run directly or reimplemented; treated as api_user based on the phrase 'CTGAN is implemented in this research'.

paper-augmentation-corrosion-dataset-def.summary: This paper proposes a data augmentation strategy for corrosion datasets of buried pipelines, using a conditional tabular GAN to generate synthetic environmental input variables and a separate machine-learning model to produce corresponding corrosion-depth outputs, then validating the merged synthetic dataset against real data with visualization and statistical metrics. The augmented dataset improves downstream corrosion-growth prediction models compared to training on the original scarce dataset alone. CTGAN, with its mode-specific normalization and conditional generator/training-by-sampling design, is run as the core generator whose hyperparameters (generator/discriminator learning rate, batch size, epochs) are tuned via Bayesian optimization, forming the whole empirical pipeline of the work.

paper-modeling-analysis-gfrp-tubular-202.summary: This paper proposes a deep meta-learning method combining optimization-based data augmentation with traditional regression models to address small-sample regression in engineering data analysis, applying it to predict the behavior of GFRP-wrapped concrete short columns and showing improved performance over SVR, GPR, and RBFNN baselines. CTGAN and its predecessor TGAN are cited only in a reference-list grouping of data augmentation techniques for expanding small datasets, with no experiment run using either.

paper-enhancing-synthetic-generation-cla.summary: This paper introduces two new synthetic tabular data generation algorithms, b-TGAN and b-TPCA, aimed at addressing class imbalance and privacy preservation respectively; b-TGAN adds a re-balancing mechanism and an autoencoder to improve minority-class representation, while b-TPCA uses only summary statistics (mean, variance, covariance) for privacy-preserving generation. The authors evaluate both methods on five datasets (Adult, Covertype, Intrusion, Credit Card Fraud, MIMIC-III) using ML utility metrics and distance-to-closest-record privacy scores. b-TGAN is explicitly built as 'an evolution of the Conditional Tabular GAN (CTGAN) framework', and default CTGAN is also run directly as the empirical baseline against which b-TGAN's class-imbalance and privacy results are measured throughout the experiments.
paper-enhancing-synthetic-generation-cla.needs: Unclear whether b-TGAN and the baseline CTGAN runs used the actual sdv-dev/CTGAN package or an authors' own reimplementation of the architecture; no explicit library/import name given.

paper-enhancing-generalization-kawasaki-.summary: This paper proposes two architectures for predicting Kawasaki Disease from imbalanced clinical data: a stacking-based Disease Classifier (DC), and a combined model (CTGAN-DC) that adds CTGAN-based oversampling to balance minority-class KD samples. The models are cross-validated on datasets from two major Taiwanese hospitals and compared against XGBoost and other baselines, with CTGAN-DC showing improved sensitivity/specificity and reduced model collapse relative to a prior JAMA model. CTGAN is run directly as the oversampling generator producing synthetic minority-class KD records, and TVAE (from the same CTGAN paper) is also run as a comparison generator (TVAE-XG).

paper-evaluation-synthetic-electronic-he.summary: A systematic review of methods for evaluating the fidelity, utility, and privacy of synthetic electronic health records, coupled with a series of original experiments probing the limitations of existing evaluation metrics (e.g., inconsistent application, qualitative bias, lack of temporal-dependency checks). The work surveys the landscape of synthetic EHR generation and evaluation methods rather than proposing a new generator itself. CTGAN is cited among the generative methods relevant to synthetic EHR production discussed in this review.
paper-evaluation-synthetic-electronic-he.needs: Full text not obtained; cannot confirm whether CTGAN was actually run in the experimental assessment or only cited as background in the review of synthetic EHR generation methods.

paper-generative-adversarial-networks-bu.summary: This is a review paper surveying generative adversarial network (GAN) variants and their applications, arguing for greater use of GANs in the field of Business Economics where research remains sparse. It surveys GAN types across domains (images, text, time-series, tabular data) and analyses the most relevant papers applying GANs to business and economic problems. CTGAN is mentioned only in passing as an example method for generating synthetic tabular data, with no experiments run.

paper-machine-learning-failure-managemen.summary: This paper proposes a Data-Centric approach for hardware-failure classification in microwave networks, using Conditional Variational Autoencoders to synthetically augment imbalanced training data and Batch Uncertainty-based Active Learning to guide data annotation. On a real-world dataset from a microwave equipment vendor, the CVAE-based augmentation is shown to outperform two state-of-the-art baselines. CTGAN is run as one of these baselines, generating synthetic minority-class samples that are compared against the authors' CVAE and against SMOTE in quantitative accuracy/F1 tables.
paper-machine-learning-failure-managemen.needs: No explicit mention of the sdv-dev package, import, or CTGAN constructor parameters; unclear whether the authors used the official SDV/CTGAN library or their own reimplementation, though the comparison is run empirically rather than merely cited.

paper-multivariate-time-series-modelling.summary: This paper introduces JDFlow, a normalizing flow method for multivariate time series generation that models a latent process via a neural SDE based on the Merton jump diffusion model, using maximum likelihood estimation to fit the Poisson intensity. It also proposes a Wasserstein-based signature quality measure to assess synthetic time series fidelity, and compares its generative results against Fourier Flow, fSDE, and PAR from SDV as baseline methods for time series generation quality.
paper-multivariate-time-series-modelling.needs: Full text not obtained; only abstract-level citing sentence available, so details of how PAR was run (library version, parameters) cannot be verified.

paper-synthetic-generation-copula-model-.summary: This paper generates synthetic vehicle driving-behavior data from CAN bus signals using a Copula model, validating it via feature-correlation comparison, K-means-based behavior classification, and a Random Forest utility/privacy trade-off analysis, reporting 98.55% privacy protection. The synthetic data generation approach is built on a copula-based model, citing the SDV-family vine copula paper as its methodological basis for the synthesizer.

paper-ctgan-dhf-varicella-covid-2024.summary: Trains decision-tree classifiers to tell dengue haemorrhagic fever, varicella and COVID-19 apart from anamnesis and examination variables drawn from an Indonesian clinic's records, comparing a model trained on duplicated real data against one trained on an equal mix of real records and CTGAN output, and reading the fitted models with SHAP to rank the contributing features. RETRACTED: the publisher has replaced the title, authors and abstract on the article page with the single word Retracted and withdrawn the PDF, while Crossref still carries the original metadata and registers no retraction notice, so nothing downstream flags it. The reported results also do not hold together, which is consistent with the withdrawal: all four confusion-matrix panels report the same 85.81 percent accuracy despite very different matrices, the abstract's headline 91.98 percent figure is a single class-precision cell rather than an accuracy, and the panel it is taken from never predicts the positive class at all. The record is kept for completeness and should not be cited. It is in the index because CTGAN is the sole generator of the synthetic half of the mixed training set, with a section of the paper devoted to CTGAN's mode-specific normalization, conditional generator and training-by-sampling and Xu et al. cited throughout for them, though no implementation library is ever named.

paper-deep-learning-iot-attack-2024.summary: This paper proposes a custom GAN-GRU architecture to generate synthetic IoT network traffic data (evaluated on UNSW-NB15) to augment training data for a Random Forest attack classifier, showing accuracy gains after merging synthetic and real samples. In its related-work discussion it describes Xu and Veeramachaneni's TGAN architecture in detail (its LSTM generator, discriminator design, and KL-divergence loss) as prior art in tabular data synthesis, and separately names CTGAN as a model it plans to adapt with a GRU-based generator in future work. Neither TGAN nor CTGAN is actually run in the reported experiments; both are cited and discussed rather than executed.
paper-deep-learning-iot-attack-2024.needs: CTGAN mention is explicitly future work, not executed in this paper; TGAN is discussed only as related-work prior art.

paper-variational-autoencoder-synthetic-.summary: This article proposes a novel Variational AutoEncoder (VAE) architecture for modelling heterogeneous insurance portfolios with mixed continuous and discrete attributes, using a quantile transformation for continuous variables and a mixed categorical-cross-entropy/MSE reconstruction loss. The authors evaluate the model's ability to reconstruct and generate synthetic motor insurance policies, addressing data-availability challenges in actuarial science. TGAN, the earlier tabular GAN work from the SDV family, is cited as prior generative-model research the authors situate their VAE approach against, but is not run in the experiments.
paper-variational-autoencoder-synthetic-.needs: Full text not obtained; cannot confirm whether TGAN is discussed as related work only or engaged with more substantively in the body.

paper-synthetic-time-series-generation-2.summary: This paper proposes AVRAE, an attention-based variational recurrent autoencoder that extends the variational evidence lower bound to time-series data for generating synthetic industrial control system (ICS) data, addressing data scarcity due to security and privacy restrictions in ICS environments. It is evaluated on the HAI ICS dataset against related generative approaches like TimeGAN and TSGAN. CTGAN is discussed only in the related-work section as prior art that models discrete and continuous tabular columns using a conditional generator, and is not run or benchmarked in the paper's own experiments.

paper-atdad-one-class-adversarial-2023.summary: This paper proposes a one-class adversarial learning framework, ATDAD, for detecting anomalies in tabular data. No abstract or full text was available to determine the method's details or experimental setup. The work cites the CTGAN paper, but the evidence does not show whether CTGAN was run, adapted, or only referenced.

paper-explainable-intelligent-cardiovasc.summary: This paper proposes an explainable diagnostic pipeline for cardiovascular disease using high-dimensional, imbalanced laboratory test results, combining a conditional tabular generative adversarial network for class-imbalance correction with a 1D CNN and self-attention module for interpretable prediction. The approach reports 88.89% diagnostic accuracy and identifies influential risk-factor features via attention weights. CTGAN is cited and applied as the generative model used to synthesize minority-class samples to address data imbalance.

paper-distributional-learning-variationa.summary: This paper proposes DistVAE, a variational autoencoder whose decoder is an infinite mixture of asymmetric Laplace distributions enabling nonparametric estimation of conditional CDFs, and applies it to synthetic tabular data generation with tunable privacy-utility tradeoff. The authors evaluate DistVAE on six tabular datasets against machine-learning utility, marginal similarity, correlation preservation, and privacy-attack metrics. CTGAN and TVAE (from the CTGAN paper) are run as two of three state-of-the-art baseline synthesizers, with the CTGAN mode-specific normalization technique discussed in the related work.

paper-crop-classification-sar-optical-ct.summary: Tackles crop-type classification from fused synthetic aperture radar and optical satellite features, where the minority crop classes have too few labelled field samples for a classifier to learn them, by synthesizing additional samples for those classes and measuring the gain in classification accuracy. The paper is a study of CTGAN itself in this setting: CTGAN is the generation method under investigation throughout, chosen for its handling of the non-Gaussian feature distributions that polarimetric and optical features produce.

paper-5g-nwdaf-anomaly-2023.summary: Examines anomaly detection inside the 5G network data analytics function, where standalone-mode deployment is new and operational traces are not yet available at scale. CTGAN generates the NWDAF records the detector trains on, an application of SDV to a telecom control plane.

paper-basiertes-akustisches-monitoring-h.summary: A German-language book chapter discussing challenges and solution approaches for AI-based acoustic monitoring in data-driven innovation, drawing on audiovisual analysis. paper-qaad-query-scalable-execution-2023.summary: This paper presents QaaD, a technique for Apache Spark that transparently converts workloads of many small queries into larger merged queries and dynamically adjusts partition sizes, achieving 10.6x to 36.6x speedups over standard Spark for small-query workloads. To evaluate scalability across dataset sizes, the authors needed larger data volumes than their real marketplace datasets provided. SDV's Gaussian copula-based model is run as an API tool to generate synthetic records that expand the benchmark datasets to larger target sizes while preserving schema and statistical properties.

paper-microbiome-disease-gans-2023.summary: Evaluates four GAN models on synthesizing microbiome-disease associations drawn from the Human Microbe Disease Association Database. CTGAN and CopulaGAN are two of the four, so half the comparison is SDV's.

paper-synthetic-generation-generative-ad.summary: This paper presents a GAN-based framework that generates synthetic burst-test data for corroded oil and gas pipelines to supplement a limited experimental dataset used to train random-forest models predicting pipeline failure risk. The authors compare models trained on real data alone versus real data combined with GAN-generated synthetic data, finding improved validation performance with the augmented dataset. The work cites TGAN (Xu & Veeramachaneni, 2018) as prior art for GAN-based tabular data synthesis underlying its generative approach.

paper-discovering-correlation-phishing-s.summary: This paper investigates the relationship between Big Five personality traits and susceptibility to phishing attacks, addressing the scarcity of real phishing-victim survey data by generating synthetic tabular records. A conditional generative adversarial network is used both to synthesize training/testing data and to classify phishing vulnerability from personality trait scores. The data-generation model is the one proposed in the CTGAN paper (Xu et al.), used to model the tabular survey data and expand the training set, though no library import or package name is mentioned.

paper-solutions-biomedical-sharing-secur.summary: This book chapter is a policy/conceptual essay on biomedical data sharing, arguing for secure computation and synthetic data generation as solutions that preserve privacy while enabling research, discussing regulatory and ethical context (GDPR, FDA, AI ethics) around synthetic data adoption. It surveys the growing evidence base showing synthetic data can yield analytical results equivalent to original datasets, citing several works as support. SDV (the Synthetic Data Vault) is cited only as one reference among several supporting the claim that synthetic data can match original data's analytical utility, with no engagement with its methods.

The abstract references prior work on synthetic data generation and cites the original SDV (Synthetic Data Vault) paper as related background, though it does not describe running the SDV toolkit itself.

paper-synthnotes-generator-framework-hig.summary: This paper presents SynthNotes, a modular framework for generating standards-compliant, privacy-preserving synthetic mental health progress notes at large scale, intended for benchmarking and training biomedical NLP and machine learning systems. It builds free-text notes from a patient-disease-physician model informed by literature and public statistical models rather than deep generative training on real data. The Synthetic Data Vault paper is cited only in a general list of prior work on synthetic data value, with no engagement with its methods.

preprint-dual-perspective-synthetic-traj.summary: This paper proposes a new framework for evaluating the utility of synthetic human mobility trajectory generators and introduces a membership inference attack against a class of these generators previously considered privacy-safe due to their resistance to trajectory-user-linking. The empirical work benchmarks trajectory-specific generative models (LSTM-TrajGAN, exGAN, TrajGDM) rather than tabular synthesizers. CTGAN is mentioned only in passing, cited as an example of GANs being applied to tabular data alongside other GAN application domains.

paper-pharmacometrics-daptomycin-2026.summary: Benchmarks synthetic generation against a daptomycin population pharmacokinetic model, asking whether synthetic patients preserve the structure a compartmental model depends on rather than only the marginals. Gaussian Copula, TVAE and CTGAN are three of five algorithms, each run to produce a hundred synthetic datasets, which is a more rigorous replication design than most of this literature.

preprint-studying-role-synthetic-machine.summary: This preprint proposes a novel synthetic-data generation method based on first-order auto-regressive noise statistics for large-scale Wi-Fi traffic forecasting, showing that ML models trained on the generated traces achieve MAE close to real-data-trained models while improving generalization by up to 50%. The Synthetic Data Vault (SDV) is mentioned only in the related-work discussion of structured (tabular/time-series) synthetic data frameworks, describing it as having demonstrated the feasibility of using ML models to replicate statistical properties of real datasets. No SDV code, model, or component is run in the paper's experiments.

paper-causal-graphs-categorical-synthesi.summary: Asks whether probabilistic causal graphs synthesise categorical data better than the general-purpose tools, on a survey of accessibility barriers, then puts the chosen synthetic set to work in an application example. Three libraries are run side by side: SDV with its Gaussian Copula synthesizer and CTGAN, DataSynthesizer with its independent and correlated attribute modes, and pyAgrum for the Bayesian network. SDV is executed as one of three co-equal arms and gets its own methods subsection.

preprint-improved-tabular-generator-vae-.summary: This paper proposes a new tabular-data synthesizer that trains a VAE conventionally and then fits a Bayesian Gaussian Mixture model to its learned latent space, instead of assuming an isotropic Gaussian prior as TVAE does. The model is validated for resemblance and ML utility on three real-world datasets, two of them medical, against CTGAN and TVAE as state-of-the-art baselines, and uses the SDV project's column/marginal-and-correlation validation technique for the resemblance evaluation. The work directly modifies TVAE's Gaussian latent-space design into a GMM-based sampling scheme while benchmarking unmodified CTGAN and TVAE as comparison points, and separately cites the original SDV paper both as a data source and for its resemblance-validation methodology.
preprint-improved-tabular-generator-vae-.needs: Not verified whether CTGAN/TVAE baselines were run via the sdv-dev/ctgan package or the authors' own reimplementation; text implies TVAE was reimplemented in-house.

preprint-generation-synthetic-gait-appli.summary: This preprint proposes a framework for turning quaternion time series of hip-rotation gait data into tabular form, and introduces a new nearest-neighbor-weighting synthetic data generator (SynGait) tailored to small, private clinical datasets, applying it to multiple sclerosis gait data. The authors benchmark SynGait against two SDV reference algorithms run with default parameters -- a copula-based synthesizer and CTGAN -- and also adopt SDV's fidelity metrics (StatisticSimilarity-type scores) to evaluate all three methods. The Synthetic Data Vault's GaussianCopula and CTGAN synthesizers, plus its evaluation metrics, are run as comparison baselines against the authors' proposed generator.

preprint-leveraging-synthetic-advance-or.summary: A methods-oriented preprint aimed at organizational science researchers, proposing a framework for generating and evaluating synthetic data to overcome barriers to data sharing (privacy, proprietary concerns, data integrity). The authors present two empirical demonstrations using GAN-based synthetic data generation on organizational datasets (a GATB assessment dataset and a leadership self-other agreement dataset), tuning hyperparameters like batch size and epochs. They explicitly used the Python SDV package to run CTGAN as the generative model producing the synthetic datasets underlying both empirical demonstrations.

preprint-review-roadmap-deep-causal-2023.summary: This is a survey paper that reviews deep causal models across three proposed data paradigms (definite, semi-definite, and indefinite data), summarizing tasks, methods, datasets, and challenges in causal discovery and representation learning with deep learning. It does not implement or run synthetic data generation methods itself. CTGAN is only listed in the bibliography as prior work on modeling tabular data with conditional GANs, with no engagement in the body text.

paper-cwdae-mixture-cramer-wold-2023.summary: Notes that a generative model trained on a joint distributional distance can score well on joint metrics while fitting individual columns poorly, and proposes a mixture Cramer-Wold distance that adds marginal reconstruction to the joint objective, so a denoising autoencoder learns both at once with a tunable trade-off. CTGAN and TVAE are two of the five synthesizers it is measured against on marginal and joint similarity, distance to closest record and attribute disclosure, all trained at the same latent dimension with their hyperparameters recorded.

paper-dp-diffusion-images-2023.summary: Shows that diffusion models can be trained under differential privacy to a standard where classifiers trained purely on their output are competitive on image benchmarks, using public pre-training, large batches and augmentation multiplicity to make private training tractable. The SDV paper and DP-CTGAN appear only in the bibliography, and CTGAN is cited once inside a list of differentially private GAN work; the paper is an image-domain study and runs nothing from the SDV family.

preprint-kaxai-integrated-environment-kn.summary: This paper presents KAXAI, an integrated software system combining AutoML, explainable-AI interpretation (via a proposed local interpreter called MEDLEY), and synthetic data generation into a single user-facing tool. For synthetic data generation the authors compare LLM-based generation, GAN-based dataset enhancement, and several Python synthetic-data libraries, finding GAN augmentation most reliable. SDV is cited for its original relational-database synthesis approach and is also run directly as one of three interchangeable Python libraries (alongside Faker and Pydbgen) for library-based synthetic data generation.

paper-adversarial-random-forests-2022.summary: Proposes adversarial random forests, which alternate between fitting a forest to discriminate real from synthetic data and resampling until the two are indistinguishable, yielding a density estimator (FORDE) and a generator (FORGE) that match deep tabular models on accuracy at a small fraction of their training cost. The real-data evaluation is Xu et al.'s tabular benchmark reproduced in full, with CTGAN and TVAE run from the SDV API implementations as two of the five deep baselines.

paper-dtai-inverse-design-2022.summary: Observes that deep generative models in engineering design optimise for statistical resemblance to the training set rather than for meeting a designer's targets, and proposes the Design Target Achievement Index, a differentiable score over multiple objectives and constraints that can be added to a generative model's loss so that sampling is steered toward feasible designs that hit the targets. CTGAN and TVAE are the two tabular generators it benchmarks against on parametric bicycle-frame data, chosen as the established state of the art for the GAN and VAE classes respectively.

preprint-time-series-transformer-generat.summary: This preprint introduces TsT-GAN, a Transformer-based GAN framework for generating synthetic time-series data that aims to jointly capture stepwise conditional distributions and the full joint distribution of sequences, benchmarked against five state-of-the-art models on five datasets. CTGAN is only listed in the introduction among prior works that apply conditional GANs to generate tabular data, with no engagement or experiments involving it. CTGAN is cited only in passing as an example of tabular-data GAN work, never run or otherwise used.

preprint-transitioning-real-synthetic-qu.summary: This workshop paper (ICLR 2021 Synthetic Data Generation Workshop) studies how synthetic-data generation techniques amplify or mitigate demographic bias in downstream classifiers, comparing standard and differentially private generators on a tabular income-prediction dataset using fairness metrics (DPD, EoD, EoP, DPR). It finds that generators producing less-correlated synthetic features (CTGAN, CopulaGAN, GaussianCopula) reduce model unfairness relative to real data, while a differentially private generator (PATE-GAN) amplifies bias. The paper explicitly uses the Synthetic Data Vault (SDV) library, running its CTGAN, GaussianCopula and CopulaGAN models as the core synthetic-data generators whose fairness impact is measured and compared against a differentially private baseline.

paper-lmte-contextual-explanations-2020.summary: Proposes LMTE, a local surrogate explainer that fits a linear model tree to synthetic data drawn around the test point, so that a single explanation carries both feature attributions and rules and can follow a non-linear decision boundary that a weighted linear surrogate cannot. CTGAN is the sampling stage the method is built on: the nearest neighbours of the test point are transformed, fed to CTGAN with the discrete columns declared, and the fitted model sampled to produce the locality the surrogate is trained on.

thesis-xu-2020.summary: The thesis version of CTGAN, with a broader benchmark against contemporary tabular generative models; the benchmarking apparatus became SDGym.

repo-ml-iss2025.summary: Slides, notebooks and exercises for a residential course on machine learning for the health sciences at Italy's Istituto Superiore di Sanità, held in November 2025. Its generative-synthesis session is SDV: `GS/CTGAN_27_11_25_adult.ipynb` builds a `Metadata`, fits a `CTGANSynthesizer` on the Adult census table, reports `run_diagnostic` and `evaluate_quality`, and closes with SDMetrics' `DisclosureProtection` and the rest of the privacy module. SDV's CTGAN and its disclosure metrics are run as the teaching example for a national public-health institute.

repo-technology-engineering.summary: Oracle's collection of demos, workshops and hands-on guides across its cloud and data-science products. The data-augmentation guide for Oracle Data Science is an SDV walkthrough, using `SingleTableMetadata` and `CTGANSynthesizer` to enhance a customer dataset. It records a vendor positioning SDV inside its own platform documentation.

repo-insidelearningmachines-blog.summary: Code examples accompanying articles on a machine-learning blog, one notebook per article. The article on unbalanced data uses `GaussianCopulaSynthesizer` with `Metadata` as one of four rebalancing techniques, so SDV is presented as an alternative to resampling rather than as the subject.
